main_text.p: stipatum & tutum, reponam te paterno solio. Tyranni mentem percepit Constantinus, & inhorruit: pallet, hæret: Tandem ira, & dolor, & indignatio, & sibi debiti, (sic censebat) Sceptri cupido, effrænem jam excusså Religione animum concitarunt in facinus: Annuit: Et tuis, inquit, ô magne Sophy, ut æquum semper duxi, parebo jussis & consiliis. Nec mora, mittit Rex, qui suo nomine præsto esse jubeant Alexandrum & Davidem Georgiæ Reges, cum manu quatuor millium è suis: Ita regni sui negotia postulare. Ubi advenêre, convivio eos accipit Constantinus lauto, Regio; Sed demum inter bellaria, quàm funestum apophoretum! Ex improviso consurgit horridus: Momento citius, & sicam stringit, & recondit eam in patris sui pectore, & rursum

page.notes: Partial text of the facing left page is visible at the left edge and is not transcribed. The last word "fum" is the catchword-like continuation "rursum" split across lines; it is printed as the line-end continuation, shown here as "rursum". Some letters in the scan are faint.
